newsitem.title: ITALY: Court orders Telecom Italia to pay damages.
newsitem.headline: Court orders Telecom Italia to pay damages.

text.p: Italian state phone operator Telecom Italia, after a three-year legal battle, has been ordered to pay 3.85 billion lire in damages to a small private phone company which challenged the group's monopoly.
Milan-based Telsystem's lawyer Davide D'Angelo Greco said a Milan appeal court made the ruling last month but the news was only released on Friday.

Telsystem, founded by Arturo Artom, claimed in 1994 that Telecom Italia refused to supply Telsystem with lines to link up its clients despite the fact that phone services in the sector had been liberalised by a European Union directive.
Italy's Antitrust authority ruled in favour of Artom's company as later did a regional industrial court and the one of the country's highest courts, the State Council.
Telsystem had begun providing its clients with cheaper connection fees than those offered by Telecom Italia, using lines leased from the latter, but Telecom Italia then removed the lines.

Telsystem was placed in liquidation in February this year. Italian newspapers said the costly legal battle had drained the company's resources, but due to the Antitrust ruling its victory over Telecom Italia helped open up the Italian telephone sector to other companies interested in challenging Telecom Italia's monopoly.
Managing Director Artom said at the time the Antitrust's favourable verdict had come too late and that his company had already lost its advantage over foreign competitors.
A spokewoman for Telecom Italia noted that the Milan court's ruling was not definitive under Italy's appeals system.
